title: Removed-feature residue
purpose: Verify that a removed feature (e.g. chapters/cold storage, EN-1945; transaction receipts, EN-1952) left no residual behavior, wire surface, configuration, deployment wiring, documentation, or vestigial test/workload branches, and that surviving behavior that previously shared code with the removed feature still works from its authoritative source.
invariants: A removed feature leaves no production code path, wire field, enum value, error reason, HTTP/OpenAPI property, CLI flag, server flag/env, operator CRD field/secret wiring, DI binding, or testserver option behind.

Surviving behavior that previously shared code with the removed feature must keep working from its authoritative source (e.g. revert planning resolves postings from TransactionState after receipt removal).
Protobuf removals realign field and enum numbering sequentially with regenerated bindings and hand-written marshal helpers in agreement; no reserved declarations are introduced (pre-release policy).
Documentation, API comparison tables, sales material, and dashboards must not describe removed behavior as current.

Tests and Antithesis workloads retain the coverage the removed feature's tests used to piggyback on (e.g. revert success/force/effective-date/already-reverted paths), and no test remains green only because its assertions became vacuous after the removal.
Unrelated uses of a removed feature's vocabulary (e.g. the English word 'receipt' meaning acknowledgement) must not be collateral-removed.
adversarial_questions: Which call sites consumed the removed symbols, and does each replacement read from the authoritative source rather than a leftover cache/sidecar?
Did any branch, helper, option, or metric become dead or unreachable because its only consumer was the removed feature?
Do generated bindings, vtproto/dethash/reader plugins, and hand-written *.pb.json.go helpers all agree on the post-removal wire shape?
Do any comments, doc pages, README trees, or operator samples still explain the removed mechanics or advertise its flags/envs?
Did the removal silently weaken a shared code path (snapshot consistency, response signing, coverage declaration) that used to be exercised through the removed feature?
Do e2e/Antithesis configurations still set environment variables or flags the server no longer parses?
dynamic_checks_to_consider: repository-wide term sweep for the removed feature's identifiers
proto field/enum contiguity verification after regeneration
revert coverage matrix without the removed input path
boot with a config that previously enabled the feature (unknown flag must fail loudly)
